createdBy: hand labelling from video frames (analysis/tools/eval_frames.py montages)

criterion.positive: a purposeful racquet-ball strike that puts the ball onto a wall: serve, rally stroke, or knock-up/warm-up drive. The stroke shows a wind-up, a contact and a follow-through, and the ball leaves toward a wall.
criterion.negative: everything else: ball bouncing on the floor with no racquet, scooping/flicking a dead ball, picking the ball up, walking or turning between points, a swing that misses, an empty court, and wall/echo transients that follow a real strike.
criterion.secondaryFlag: inPlay = the strike is part of live play (serve or rally exchange) as opposed to knock-up / between-point practice hitting.
criterion.confidence: high = the swing and its follow-through are unambiguous; med = the stroke is clear but the exact contact frame or the ball is not; low = a guess, EXCLUDED from the headline metrics.

note: Contact times are read off frames sampled every 0.2 s (strips) or 0.08-0.25 s (zooms), so they carry about +/-0.08 s of timing error - well inside the 0.3 s match tolerance. strikerBox is the colour of the engine's tracked box (GREEN=A, MAGENTA=B) drawn on the striker in the frame that was looked at; strikerLook is the striker's appearance, which is what identifies the human. The two disagree wherever the identity tracker has swapped.
